mainTopic: יש אם למקרא versus יש אם למסורת: whether the reading aloud or the spelling of a פסוק decides the הלכה
overview: The גמרא finishes the debate over the word ירשיען. רבי learns from its plural pronunciation that monetary cases need several judges, and the רבנן answer that the written letters can be read as singular. רבי יוחנן then names five תנאים who all hold יש אם למקרא, meaning the way a פסוק is read aloud decides the הלכה: רבי, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית שמאי, רבי שמעון and רבי עקיבא. The גמרא proves each one. רבי יהודה בן רועץ reads 'two weeks', not 'seventy', for the impurity of a mother after a girl. בית שמאי count six 'horns' for a חטאת, while בית הלל count four by the spelling. רבי שמעון counts the walls of a סוכה by the reading, while the רבנן count by the spelling. רבי עקיבא reads נפשת as plural, so blood from two dead people joins together. At the end, רב אחא בר יעקב challenges the whole idea by asking whether anyone really rejects יש אם למקרא, and he starts quoting a ברייתא about בחלב אמו that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Rabbis answer: the word is written in a way that can be singular
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי's proof from ירשיען, because the written form can be read as singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say: 'ירשיען' is written (in a way that can be read as singular).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן answer רבי's proof that monetary cases need more than one judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי relied on how ירשיען is pronounced, which is plural ('they shall condemn'), so it implies several judges. The רבנן point out that the written letters can also be read as singular ('he shall condemn him'). They follow the written form, so there is no proof of a plural.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
It is written, meaning how the letters appear in the Torah
'Shall condemn,' from שמות 22:8. It is pronounced as plural, but the written form can be read as singular

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how do they respond?
"Shall condemn" is written (in a form that can be read as singular).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's proof from the previous section of the daf
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reading of the פסוק based on its written form
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ירשיען is pronounced as plural, it would prove that several judges are needed
steps.terutzMaskana: The written form can be singular, so the רבנן do not accept the proof

steps.title: Five תנאים all hold that the reading aloud is what counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists רבי, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית שמאי, רבי שמעון and רבי עקיבא as all holding יש אם למקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית שמאי, רבי שמעון and רבי עקיבא all hold that the way the פסוק is read aloud is the authoritative basis.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן turns the debate about ירשיען into a general principle and names five תנאים who all follow the reading aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between רבי and the רבנן is really about a wider question: do we learn הלכה from how a word is pronounced (יש אם למקרא) or from how its letters are written (יש אם למסורת)? רבי יוחנן says that these five תנאים all go by the pronunciation. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא proves each name.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading aloud (pronunciation) is the 'root,' the authoritative basis for halacha
The opposite view: the written letters are the authoritative basis
All of them
They hold, they are of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' by itself means רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not a general title for any rabbi.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle comes up all over ש"ס. Knowing that the debate is about pronunciation versus spelling helps explain many arguments built on single words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosei said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi, and Rabbi Yehuda ben Roetz,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא –
phrases.english: and Beit Shammai, and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Akiva:
all of them hold
that the reading aloud is authoritative.
phrases.notes: Literally 'there is a mother to the reading.' The pronunciation is the 'mother,' the source we learn from.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific ירשיען debate into a general principle
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית שמאי, רבי שמעון and רבי עקיבא all hold יש אם למקרא

steps.title: The source for רבי: what was just said
steps.stepSummary: רבי's view comes from his reading of ירשיען as plural, which was just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי: this is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving רבי יוחנן's list one name at a time, beginning with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new source is needed for רבי. He learned that several judges are needed from the pronounced plural of ירשיען. That shows he follows the reading aloud, which is יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we just said
'Whom the judges shall condemn,' the פסוק רבי relied on

phrases.english: Rabbi: that which we just said.
phrases.notes: This points back to his proof from ירשיען that monetary cases need several judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first name on רבי יוחנן's list
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds יש אם למקרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: His reading of ירשיען as plural, discussed earlier on the daf

steps.title: The source for רבי יהודה בן רועץ: the students' question about 'seventy'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought. Students ask רבי יהודה בן רועץ whether the written letters of the word for 'two weeks' could be read as 'seventy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה בן רועץ, as a ברייתא teaches: The students asked רבי יהודה בן רועץ: I can read the word as 'seventy.' Perhaps a woman who gives birth to a girl should be impure for seventy days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving the second name with a ברייתא. This step only sets up the students' question. The next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 12:5 the word is pronounced שבועים, 'two weeks,' but it is written without a ו, so the letters could also be read שבעים, 'seventy.' If the written form counted, a mother of a girl would be impure for seventy days. His answer will show that he goes by the pronunciation, which supports רבי יוחנן's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventy, a possible reading of the written letters
Two weeks, the way the word is actually pronounced
One might think, which introduces a possible but mistaken conclusion
A woman who gives birth to a girl

steps.confusionAlert: The students are not really suggesting seventy days. They are testing whether the written letters can override the pronunciation. Steps 5 and 6 give his answer.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda ben Roetz, as it is taught in a baraita:
The students asked
Rabbi Yehuda ben Roetz:
I can read it as "seventy,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5. The word for 'two weeks' is written without a ו, so the letters can also spell 'seventy.'

phrases.english: so one might think that a woman who gives birth to a girl
is impure for seventy days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second name on רבי יוחנן's list
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן רועץ holds יש אם למקרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the impurity period after giving birth to a girl (ויקרא 12:5). His answer comes in steps 5 and 6

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן רועץ proves the impurity period is doubled, not seventy days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן רועץ answers his students with a comparison. The Torah doubles the טהרה period for a girl, so the טומאה period must also be doubled: two weeks, not seventy days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The Torah made her impure and pure after a boy, and impure and pure after a girl. When it made her pure after a boy, the period after a girl is double. So too, when it made her impure after a boy, the period after a girl is double.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן רועץ answers the students' question from the previous step. He uses logic to show that the word must mean 'two weeks,' not 'seventy.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a boy, a יולדת has 7 days of טומאה and 33 days of טהרה. For a girl, the טהרה days are doubled to 66. So the טומאה days should also be doubled, to 14 days, which matches 'two weeks' and not 'seventy.'

keyTerms.meaning: made impure (the Torah declared her טמאה)
made pure (the Torah declared her טהורה)
a male / a female (the baby she gave birth to)
double

phrases.english: He said to them: [The Torah] made [her] impure and pure for a male,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה בן רועץ, answering his students' question about 'seventy.'

phrases.english: and made [her] impure and pure for a female.
Just as when it made [her] pure for a male,
for a female it is double,
phrases.notes: 33 days of purity after a boy become 66 after a girl.

phrases.english: so too, when it made [her] impure for a male,
for a female it is double.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 4 about reading 'two weeks' as 'seventy.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could the written letters be read as 'seventy,' making the טומאה period seventy days?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. By comparing to the doubled טהרה period, the טומאה period is also doubled: 14 days, two weeks.

steps.title: The real reason: we follow how the word is read
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן רועץ runs after his students to say his logical proof is not needed. The word is read 'שבועיים,' and the reading is what counts: יש אם למקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they left, he went out and ran after them. He said to them: You do not need this proof. We read the word as 'two weeks,' and the reading is authoritative.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן רועץ takes back his need for the logical proof and gives the simple reason instead. This is why רבי יוחנן listed him as holding יש אם למקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first answer relied on logic. His final answer relies only on the reading tradition: the word is read 'שבועיים,' and the reading decides the meaning, not the bare letters. This proves he holds יש אם למקרא, as רבי יוחנן said in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: need, depend on
we read (the word is pronounced this way)
the way a word is read (its vowels) is the authoritative basis for learning from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן רועץ ends up proving 'two weeks' from the reading of the word alone. That shows he holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the logical 'double' proof is his real source. He himself says it is not needed. The reading of the word is what decides.

phrases.english: After they left, he went out and went after them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אִי אַתֶּם זְקוּקִים לְכָךְ.
phrases.english: He said to them: You do not need this.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the 'double' proof he just gave.

phrases.english: We read 'two weeks,'
and the reading is authoritative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the logical proof of step 5 with a simpler reason based on the reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה בן רועץ holds יש אם למקרא: 'two weeks' comes straight from how the word is read.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about blood presentations on the altar
steps.stepSummary: To show that בית שמאי hold יש אם למקרא, the גמרא quotes a משנה. בית שמאי say one מתנה is enough for most קרבנות on the outer מזבח, but a חטאת needs two. בית הלל say one is enough even for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: About בית שמאי, as we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say: For all blood placed on the outer altar, if it was placed with one placement, it atoned, as it says: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out.' But a חטאת needs two placements. And בית הלל say: Even a חטאת placed with one placement atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next name on רבי יוחנן's list, בית שמאי. It first quotes the משנה that will be the basis for the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of disagreement is the חטאת: בית שמאי require at least two מתנות to be valid, while בית הלל accept one. The גמרא will soon show that בית שמאי's 'two' comes from reading the פסוקים, which is why they hold יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: the outer altar, in the courtyard
one placement of blood on the altar
it atoned, meaning the קרבן is valid
sin-offering

phrases.english: Beit Shammai, as we learned:
Beit Shammai say,
all [bloods] that are placed on the outer altar
that one placed with one placement, it atoned,
as it says: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured out.'
But with a sin-offering, two placements.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּחַטָּאת שֶׁנְּתָנָן בְּמַתָּנָה אַחַת – כִּיפֵּר.
phrases.english: Even a sin-offering that one placed with one placement, it atoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהודה בן רועץ and moves to the next name on רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold יש אם למקרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים about how many מתנות a חטאת needs.

steps.title: רב הונא explains בית שמאי's source: six horns
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the word 'קרנת' appears three times for the חטאת. Read as plural, each one means two, which makes six: four for the ideal מצוה and two that are required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: What is the reason of בית שמאי? 'Horns,' 'horns,' 'horns.' Here there are six: four for the מצוה, and two to make it required.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the source for בית שמאי's rule that a חטאת needs two מתנות. This sets up the proof that בית שמאי follow how the word is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of six only works if each 'קרנת' is read as plural, meaning at least two horns. Four horns are the ideal way, and the extra two are the minimum that makes the קרבן valid. So בית שמאי's rule depends on the reading of the word, which ties them to יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
horns, the corners of the altar
for the ideal way to do it
required: without it, the קרבן is not valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key step for showing that בית שמאי hold יש אם למקרא. Their rule rests on reading 'קרנת' as plural each time.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
What is the reason of Beit Shammai?
'Horns,' 'horns,' 'horns':
here there are six:
phrases.notes: Each plural 'horns' means at least two, so three times two makes six.

phrases.english: four for the מצוה, and two to be required.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind בית שמאי's rule from the משנה in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי learn from three plural 'קרנת' that there are six horns: four for the ideal מצוה and two that are required, so a חטאת needs two מתנות.

steps.title: בית הלל count the horns by spelling
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל count by how the word is written: one full plural and two singulars make four. Three are for the ideal מצוה and one is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: 'horns' (spelled as a plural), 'horn,' 'horn': that makes four. Three are for the ideal מצוה, and one is required.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his explanation by giving בית הלל's count. They go by the spelling, not the reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the written Torah, 'קרנות' is spelled once with a ו, so it is plural and means two. The other two times it is spelled without a ו, so each one can mean just one horn. Two plus one plus one makes four, so only one placement is required, which fits בית הלל's ruling that one מתנה is enough even for a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Horns, meaning the corners of the מזבח
For the ideal way of doing it, but not required after the fact
Required. Without it, the קרבן does not work

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two counts. בית שמאי (step 8) count by the reading and get six, so two are required. בית הלל count by the spelling and get four, so only one is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בית הלל hold יש אם למסורת, the spelling is the root. That is the opposite of בית שמאי.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
"Horns" (spelled as a plural), "horn," "horn"
here there are four.
Three are for the ideal מצוה,
and one is required.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: קַרְנוֹת, קַרְנַת, קַרְנַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's explanation by giving בית הלל's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל count by spelling and get four placements: three for the ideal מצוה and one required.

steps.title: Why not say all four are only for the ideal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית הלל need any required placement. Maybe all four are just for the ideal מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say that all of them are only for the ideal מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית הלל's split of three for the ideal and one required. Why not make all four optional?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the count of four forces one of them to be required. If all four were only for the ideal, the קרבן would work even with no blood placed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead. Used to suggest a different reading
All of them

phrases.english: But say: all of them are for the מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the split that בית הלל made in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's claim that one of the four placements is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The count of four does not show that any placement is required. All four could be just for the ideal.

steps.title: No atonement without any blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we never find atonement with no blood placed at all. So at least one placement must be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have never found atonement with nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A קרבן cannot bring atonement if no blood was placed, so one placement must be required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making all four optional would mean the קרבן works with zero blood, and that has no example anywhere in the Torah. So at least one placement has to be required, and the other three are for the ideal.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
For nothing, with no action at all
We have not found

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: four placements by the spelling. Three are for the ideal, and one is required, because there is no atonement without any blood.

phrases.english: Atonement with nothing at all
phrases.notes: He means a קרבן that atones even though no blood was put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: we have not found!

steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four placements could be just for the ideal.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קרבן never atones with no blood, so one placement must be required.

steps.title: רבי שמעון and the walls of a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The next example of someone who holds יש אם למקרא is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows that he argues with the רבנן about how many walls a סוכה needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון, as a ברייתא teaches: a סוכה needs two proper walls, and the third can be even one טפח. רבי שמעון says: three proper walls, and the fourth can be even one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another example: רבי שמעון. It quotes a ברייתא about סוכה walls, which will show what he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require two full walls and a small third. רבי שמעון requires three full walls and a small fourth. The ברייתא gives only the rulings. The reason behind them comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: In their proper, full form
A handbreadth, a small measure
The hut used on סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught:
Two walls in their proper form,
and the third even a handbreadth.
Rabbi Shimon says:
three in their proper form,
and the fourth even a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After בית שמאי, the גמרא brings a new example of someone who holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds יש אם למקרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the number of walls a סוכה needs

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the רבנן and רבי שמעון are arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next step. The גמרא asks for the principle behind the argument about סוכה walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only the rulings. The גמרא wants the reason under them, so it can tie the argument back to the spelling versus reading question.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they argue?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle behind the argument between the רבנן and רבי שמעון

steps.title: Spelling versus reading
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold יש אם למסורת, the spelling is the root. רבי שמעון holds יש אם למקרא, the reading is the root.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that the written spelling is the root, and רבי שמעון holds that the reading is the root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סוכה argument comes from the spelling versus reading question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that רבי שמעון belongs on the list of people who hold יש אם למקרא. The רבנן take the other side and follow the written letters.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling (the letters) is the root of the meaning
The way the word is read (the vowels) is the root of the meaning

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מסורת' does not mean tradition in general. It means the way the letters are written in the Torah, full or missing a ו.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: the written spelling is the root,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon holds: the reading is the root.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן follow the spelling, and רבי שמעון follows the reading.

steps.title: How the רבנן count the סוכה walls
steps.stepSummary: Going by spelling, 'בסכת' twice plus 'בסכות' once makes four. Take one away for the basic מצוה and three are left. A הלכה למשה מסיני shrinks the third to one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold the spelling is the root. 'בסכת,' 'בסכת,' 'בסכות': that makes four. Take away one פסוק for the מצוה itself, and three are left. The הלכה came, reduced the third, and set it at one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows step by step how the רבנן get their ruling of two full walls and a third of one טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two singular spellings (1+1) plus one plural spelling (2) make four. One mention is used to teach the basic מצוה of living in a סוכה, which leaves three walls. A הלכה למשה מסיני then makes the third wall only one טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove, take away
For itself, to teach the basic מצוה
A הלכה למשה מסיני, a law given orally to משה
It reduced it
And it set it

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן follow the spelling: four, minus one for the מצוה, leaves three walls, and the third is cut to one טפח. רבי שמעון follows the reading: six, minus two, leaves four walls, and the fourth is one טפח.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: the written spelling is the root.
"In sukkat," "in sukkat," "in sukkot"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:42-43. Two are spelled without a ו (one each), and one with a ו (two). Together that makes four.

phrases.english: here there are four.
Take away one verse for itself,
three are left.
The halakha came,
reduced the third,
and set it at a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in detail how the רבנן's principle from step 14 produces their ruling from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By the spelling there are four. One is used for the מצוה, three walls are left, and the הלכה makes the third one טפח.

steps.title: How רבי שמעון counts the walls of a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads all three words as plural (בַּסֻּכּוֹת), which gives six walls. Take away two for the basic מצוה and four are left. A הלכה למשה מסיני shrinks the fourth wall to one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds: the word is read 'in sukkos' three times, and each plural means two, so that makes six. Take away one פסוק for the basic מצוה and four are left. The הלכה came and shrank the fourth wall, setting it at one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's side of the סוכה argument. He counts walls by how the word is read, not by how it is spelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word read as plural counts for two walls, so three words make six. One פסוק is used for the basic מצוה, which removes two, leaving four. The הלכה למשה מסיני makes the last wall only one טפח, so רבי שמעון ends up with three full walls and a small fourth.

keyTerms.meaning: Take away, remove from the count
For itself, to teach the basic מצוה
Are left over, remain
Reduced it, made it smaller
A handbreadth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two counts. The רבנן (step 15) end with three walls where the third is only a טפח. רבי שמעון ends with four walls where the fourth is only a טפח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
'in sukkos,' 'in sukkos,' 'in sukkos'
phrases.notes: All three are read as plurals, and each plural counts as two walls.

phrases.english: so there are six here.
Take away one verse for the מצוה itself,
phrases.notes: That פסוק is read as a plural too, so taking it away removes two walls.

phrases.english: and four are left.
The הלכה came and reduced the fourth wall,
and set it at one handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's count, matching the רבנן's count in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following the reading, the פסוקים yield four walls, and the fourth is reduced to a טפח

steps.title: רבי עקיבא also follows the reading: blood from two dead people
steps.stepSummary: The next example of יש אם למקרא is רבי עקיבא. He learns from the plural reading 'נַפְשֹׁת' that a רביעית of blood from two dead people still makes things impure in a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא, as taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says, how do we know that a רביעית of blood that came out of two dead people makes things impure in a tent? Because the פסוק says 'He shall not come upon any souls of the dead.' That means two souls and one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another sage, רבי עקיבא, who follows the way a word is read. It quotes a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'נַפְשֹׁת' is read as plural, 'souls.' Blood is treated as the 'soul,' so רבי עקיבא learns that blood from two people can join together to make one full measure. His rule depends on reading the word as plural.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, the amount of blood that makes things impure
Makes people and things impure when they are under the same roof
Souls, here read as plural
A required measure or amount

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Akiva says,
from where do we know that a quarter-log of blood
that came out of two dead people
makes things impure in a tent?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כׇּל נַפְשֹׁת מֵת לֹא יָבֹא״ –
phrases.english: As it says: 'He shall not come upon any souls of the dead'
two souls, and one measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sage to the list of those who hold יש אם למקרא
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds יש אם למקרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'נַפְשֹׁת' as plural to include blood from two dead people

steps.title: The רבנן go by the spelling of נפשת
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that 'נפשת' is spelled without a ו, so it can be read as one soul. Blood from two dead people does not join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: 'נפשת' is written without a ו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: the רבנן go by the spelling. That is why they disagree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ו, the letters can be read as the singular 'נַפְשַׁת,' one soul. So for the רבנן, a רביעית of blood only makes things impure if it came from one dead person.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written, meaning how the word is spelled

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern repeats in every example: the sage who follows the reading holds יש אם למקרא, and the רבנן who follow the spelling hold יש אם למסורת.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
'נפשת' is what is written.
phrases.notes: It is spelled without a ו, so it can be read as one soul and not many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the רבנן's spelling-based view against רבי עקיבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spelling 'נפשת' means one soul, so blood from two dead people does not combine

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב asks: doesn't everyone follow the reading?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges the whole approach. He asks whether any sage really rejects יש אם למקרא, and he starts quoting a ברייתא about 'בחלב אמו' to show that everyone follows the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב challenged this: is there anyone who does not hold that the reading is the root? But a ברייתא teaches: 'in its mother's milk.' One might think it means 'in fat'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the idea that these arguments are about reading against spelling. He begins bringing a ברייתא as his proof, and the proof continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters חלב can be read as 'milk' (חָלָב) or 'fat' (חֵלֶב). The ברייתא raises the 'fat' option only to reject it, which suggests everyone goes by the traditional reading 'milk.' If so, no one would hold יש אם למסורת, and the explanation of all these arguments falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, raised a strong objection
The reading is the root and decides the meaning
In its mother's milk
One might have thought
Fat

steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the whole explanation that these arguments come from reading against spelling would be in danger.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov challenged it:
Is there anyone who does not hold
'the reading is the root'?
But wasn't it taught: 'in its mother's milk'
one might think it means 'in the fat'?
phrases.notes: The same letters חלב can be read as milk or as fat. The ברייתא keeps going in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: מִי אִיכָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from listing examples to challenging the whole framework
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן in these arguments hold יש אם למסורת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about meat and milk seems to show that everyone follows the reading, so no one would hold יש אם למסורת
